headers._comment: Everything defaults to revalidate-before-use. Without this, Firebase serves index.html with max-age=3600, so for an hour after every deploy returning visitors keep running the OLD bundle - the new one is on the CDN but nothing asks for it. SPA routes like /donate have no file extension, so only a '**' rule reaches them.
Listed after the catch-all so it wins for these. Vite fingerprints these filenames, so a changed file is a NEW url and can be cached forever - the stale-deploy problem above cannot apply to them.

/sw.js ends in .js, so without this it would fall under the immutable-forever rule just above - exactly wrong for a service worker script, which is NOT fingerprinted (public/sw.js is always exactly that URL) and needs to be re-fetched and diffed on every visit for a deploy to ever reach a returning visitor. Chrome does cap a service worker's own re-check interval at 24h regardless of Cache-Control, but that is a browser-vendor safety net for sites that get this wrong, not something to depend on deliberately.

Security headers, on every response. CSP origins are scoped to what this app actually loads: Google Fonts (index.html), Firebase Auth's REST calls (identitytoolkit/securetoken/googleapis) plus its Google Sign-In popup flow - apis.google.com (the gapi/GIS loader script - a real, deployed CSP violation caught live: apis.google.com/js/api.js got silently blocked, found by chance while checking dark mode, not by testing sign-in directly), accounts.google.com for the OAuth handshake itself (the popup's own page content is a separate top-level navigation not subject to this page's CSP, but the opener page's iframe/script/connect activity during that flow is), and *.firebaseapp.com kept as a fallback even though authDomain (frontend/.env) now points at this app's own short Hosting site ecotrk.web.app (hosting.site below) - Firebase's hidden auth-state iframe is same-origin as a result, which is why frame-src also needs 'self' explicitly: an explicit frame-src directive is NOT backfilled with default-src's 'self', so without this the app's own auth iframe would be the one thing this policy blocked. Two separate Console-only registrations are required whenever authDomain points at a new Hosting site, confirmed the hard way across two different live breaks: (1) Google Cloud Console > Google Auth Platform > Clients > the Web OAuth client Firebase Auth uses - add the new domain as an Authorized JavaScript origin and /__/auth/handler as an Authorized redirect URI, or sign-in fails with Error 400 redirect_uri_mismatch after redirecting to Google; (2) Firebase Console > Authentication > Settings > Authorized domains - add the new domain there too, or the /__/auth/handler page itself fails with 'The requested action is invalid' before ever reaching Google (Hosting sites under a project are NOT auto-added here despite being auto-authorized for Hosting itself). Both were done for ecotrk.web.app and verified live: accounts.google.com reads 'to continue to ecotrk.web.app' with no error. The Flask API on Vercel (utils/api.js baseURL - CORS_ORIGINS on Vercel must also list the new frontend origin), Unsplash-hosted photos (utils/photos.js), Pexels-hosted hero video + poster (components/HeroReel.jsx - also caught live, not by desk research), Razorpay's checkout script + its own API calls (utils/razorpay.js, Donate.jsx) - donations open Razorpay's UI inside an iframe/popup it manages itself, hence frame-src - and Google reCAPTCHA v3 (utils/recaptcha.js), which loads its own script from google.com and runs its verification inside a hidden iframe regardless of whether the visible badge is shown. style-src keeps 'unsafe-inline': this app is built with inline style={{...}} throughout every component, and CSP's style-src covers the style attribute as well as
